# Introduction

The [Human Tumor Atlas Network](https://humantumoratlas.org) (HTAN) is an
NCI Cancer Moonshot program that built multi-modal atlases of human cancers:
single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, multiplexed imaging, bulk
sequencing, and the clinical and biospecimen data that tie them together.
Phase 1 is complete; its final data release, Release 7, came out in
November 2025.

*HTAN* is a client for the open-access part of HTAN Phase 1. It does four
things:

1. **Query** file, biospecimen, clinical and provenance metadata locally,
   with dplyr, from a parquet snapshot of the ISB-CGC HTAN release tables.
   No Google account is needed.
2. **Trace lineage**: from a processed file back to the raw files, the
   biospecimens and the participant it came from.
3. **Download** open files: Level 2 imaging anonymously from the CRDC
   General Commons, and Level 3/4 processed data from Synapse with a free
   account.
4. **Read** HTAN file formats into Bioconductor classes
   (`SingleCellExperiment`, `SpatialExperiment`, `MultiAssayExperiment`).

Controlled-access data (Level 1/2 sequencing, dbGaP phs002371) is out of
scope.

# Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("seandavi/HTAN")
```

```{r load, message = FALSE}
library(HTAN)
library(dplyr)
```

# Connecting to a snapshot

All metadata comes from one DuckDB connection over a versioned snapshot.
`htan_con()` reads the snapshot's `manifest.json`, caches and checks each
parquet file, and creates one SQL view per table. Every other function uses
that connection.

By default `htan_con("r7")` reads the public Hugging Face dataset
[`seandavis/htan`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/seandavis/htan) (tag
`r7`, about 20 MB of parquet), checks every file against the manifest's
sha256, and caches it. The dataset page also has a viewer and a SQL console
for browsing the same tables without R.

```{r hf-snapshot, eval = FALSE}
con <- htan_con("r7")   # downloads once, then reads from the cache
```

The location can be changed with `options(HTAN.base_url = ...)`. The package
ships a tiny fixture of the r7 snapshot (all 78 tables, restricted to six
participants), which this vignette uses so it runs offline:

```{r con}
fixture <- system.file("extdata", "snapshot", package = "HTAN")
options(HTAN.base_url = fixture)
con <- htan_con("r7")
htan_snapshot_info(con)[c("release", "phase", "source", "fixture")]
```

For real work, drop the option (or set it to a mirror or a local build from
`inst/scripts/build_snapshot`):

```{r full-snapshot, eval = FALSE}
options(HTAN.base_url = NULL)   # back to the Hugging Face default
con <- htan_con("r7")
```

# Exploring tables

`htan_tables()` lists the snapshot's tables, with the ISB-CGC table each was
exported from. `htan_tbl()` opens one as a lazy table: dplyr verbs run in
DuckDB until `collect()`.

```{r tables}
htan_tables(con)
htan_tbl("clinical_tier1_demographics", con) |>
    select(HTAN_Participant_ID, Gender, Race, Ethnicity) |>
    collect()
```

Column descriptions come from the BigQuery schema:

```{r columns}
htan_columns("id_provenance", con) |>
    select(column, description)
```

# Finding files

`htan_files()` has one row per HTAN data file, combining all of HTAN's
file-level tables. It adds the assay and level, the file extension, the
participants and biospecimens the file was derived from, the General Commons
DRS ID, and an `access` tier that says how the file can be fetched.

```{r files}
files <- htan_files(con = con)
files |>
    count(assay, level, access) |>
    arrange(assay, level) |>
    collect()
```

Filters can be given directly. Here are the processed (Level 4) single-cell
files, and everything derived from one participant:

```{r files-filter}
htan_files(assay == "ScRNA-seq", level == 4, con = con) |>
    select(HTAN_Data_File_ID, extension, File_Size, HTAN_Participant_ID) |>
    collect()

htan_files(participants = "HTA7_1005", con = con) |>
    select(HTAN_Data_File_ID, Component, extension, File_Size, access) |>
    collect()
```

A few percent of files (for example, merged single-cell objects) come from
several participants. Their `HTAN_Participant_ID` is comma-separated, which is
why the `participants` argument is the reliable way to filter by participant.

# Tracing lineage

`htan_lineage()` follows `id_provenance` from a file to the files it was
derived from (negative depth) or to its descendants (positive depth).

```{r lineage}
l4 <- htan_files(assay == "ScRNA-seq", level == 4,
    participants = "HTA12_251", con = con) |>
    head(1)
htan_lineage(l4, con = con) |>
    select(related_file_id, depth, Component, HTAN_Assayed_Biospecimen_ID) |>
    arrange(depth) |>
    collect()
```

# Downloading files

`htan_download()` routes each file by its `access` tier:

* `open-gc`: open Level 2 imaging, fetched anonymously from the CRDC
  General Commons with GA4GH DRS;
* `open-synapse`: Level 3/4 processed data, fetched from Synapse with a
  personal access token;
* `controlled`: refused, with a pointer to dbGaP.

Files are checked against their md5. A size guard (`max_bytes`, 20 GB by
default) stops accidental downloads of very large images; the Orion image
above is 55 GB.

An open imaging file needs no account. This 250 KB imaging mass cytometry
image downloads anonymously (the chunk tolerates being offline):

```{r download-gc}
tiff <- htan_files(drs_uri == "dg.4DFC/6231a7d4-7e68-11ee-b51d-e7db3b9207b8",
    con = con)
dl <- tryCatch(
    htan_download(tiff, dest = tempfile("htan-"), con = con),
    error = function(e) {
        message("Download skipped: ", conditionMessage(e))
        NULL
    }
)
dl
```

Processed files are on Synapse. Create a free account at
<https://www.synapse.org>, make a personal access token (Account Settings >
Personal Access Tokens), and put it in `SYNAPSE_AUTH_TOKEN`, for example in
`~/.Renviron`:

```{r download-synapse, eval = FALSE}
Sys.setenv(SYNAPSE_AUTH_TOKEN = "<your token>")
h5ad <- htan_files(assay == "ScRNA-seq", level == 4, extension == ".h5ad",
    participants = "HTA5_1470", con = con)
dl <- htan_download(h5ad, dest = "htan-data", con = con)
sce <- read_htan(dl)
```

# Reading files

`read_htan()` dispatches on the file extension:

| file | returns |
|---|---|
| `.h5ad` | `SingleCellExperiment` (via anndataR), or `SpatialExperiment` with a spatial embedding |
| `.rds`, `.RData` | the object; Seurat objects become `SingleCellExperiment` |
| 10x `.h5` | `SingleCellExperiment` (via TENxIO) |
| Space Ranger `outs/` | `SpatialExperiment` (via VisiumIO) |
| imaging Level 4 `.csv` cell table | `SpatialExperiment` |
| `.tif`, `.ome.tiff`, `.svs` | the path (use RBioFormats or cytomapper) |

The downloaded image is returned as a path:

```{r read-image}
if (!is.null(dl)) read_htan(dl)
```

Imaging Level 4 files are cell-by-feature tables: one row per segmented
cell, with marker intensities, centroids and morphology. Here is a small
synthetic table in the MCMICRO layout used by several HTAN centers:

```{r read-cells}
cells <- data.frame(
    CellID = 1:5,
    CD3 = c(8.1, 0.2, 7.5, 0.1, 6.9),
    CD20 = c(0.3, 9.2, 0.1, 8.8, 0.2),
    PanCK = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.1, 9.9),
    X_centroid = c(101, 240, 130, 410, 520),
    Y_centroid = c(88, 95, 300, 310, 120),
    Area = c(51, 63, 48, 70, 120)
)
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
write.csv(cells, path, row.names = FALSE)
spe <- read_htan(path)
spe
SpatialExperiment::spatialCoords(spe)
```

Centroid columns are detected from common names; pass `coords =` when a
center uses others.

# Assembling a MultiAssayExperiment

`htan_experiment()` combines objects read from HTAN files into a
`MultiAssayExperiment`. The `sampleMap` links every cell or spot to its
participant through `id_provenance`, and `colData` holds the participants'
demographics and diagnosis. Name each object by the file it came from:

```{r experiment}
orion <- htan_files(participants = "HTA7_1005", level == 4, con = con) |>
    pull(HTAN_Data_File_ID)
mae <- htan_experiment(setNames(list(spe), orion), con = con)
mae
MultiAssayExperiment::colData(mae)[, c("Gender", "Primary_Diagnosis",
    "Tissue_or_Organ_of_Origin")]
```

For a file derived from several participants, pass `participant_col`: the
`colData` column that holds each cell's participant or biospecimen ID.

# Building the snapshot

Maintainers rebuild the snapshot from ISB-CGC BigQuery with the uv project in
`inst/scripts/build_snapshot`. It needs Google credentials and a billing
project, dry-runs first, and stops if the estimate exceeds 5 GB (an r7 build
bills under 1 GB):

```{sh build, eval = FALSE}
just snapshot <gcp-project>    # writes snapshot/r7/*.parquet + manifest.json
just fixture                   # re-cuts inst/extdata/snapshot from it
```

# Session information

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
htan_disconnect()
```

```{r sessionInfo}
sessionInfo()
```
